title: An equivalence of sites preserving and reflecting coverings and its quasi-inverse define morphisms of sites
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal C$ be sites in the sense of Stacks Sites, Definition 00VH [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1). Let $p:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ be an equivalence of categories such that a family $\{X_a\to X\}_{a\in I}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal A$ with common target is a covering of $\mathcal A$ if and only if $\{p(X_a)\to p(X)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. Let $p':\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ be a quasi-inverse, with natural isomorphisms $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}\cong p'\circ p$ and $\varepsilon:p\circ p'\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$. Then: (1) a family $\{Y_a\to Y\}_{a\in I}$ of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$ if and only if $\{p'(Y_a)\to p'(Y)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal A$; (2) $p$ and $p'$ are continuous (Sites, Definition 00WV, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)); (3) the functors $p^s:\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G\circ p$ from sheaves of sets (resp. abelian sheaves) on $\mathcal C$ to those on $\mathcal A$ and $p'^s:\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F\circ p'$ in the other direction are quasi-inverse equivalences of categories; (4) $p_s$ and $p'_s$ on sheaves of sets are exact, so $p$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ and $p'$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ (Sites, Definition 00X1), and $p_s$ is a quasi-inverse of $p^s$, $p'_s$ a quasi-inverse of $p'^s$.

proof.text: *Step 1 (clause (1); symmetry of the hypotheses).* Let $\{g_a:Y_a\to Y\}_{a\in I}$ be a family of morphisms of $\mathcal C$ with common target. By the hypothesis on $p$, applied to the family $\{p'(g_a):p'(Y_a)\to p'(Y)\}_{a\in I}$ of $\mathcal A$, this family is a covering of $\mathcal A$ if and only if $\{pp'(g_a):pp'(Y_a)\to pp'(Y)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$. By naturality of $\varepsilon$, $g_a\circ\varepsilon_{Y_a}=\varepsilon_Y\circ pp'(g_a)$ for every $a$, with $\varepsilon_{Y_a},\varepsilon_Y$ isomorphisms. If $\{g_a\}$ is a covering, [lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-isomorphic-family] with $U_a=Y_a$, $U=Y$, $f_a=pp'(g_a)$, $\sigma_a=\varepsilon_{Y_a}$, $\varphi=\varepsilon_Y$ shows that $\{pp'(g_a)\}$ is a covering. Conversely, if $\{pp'(g_a)\}$ is a covering, the same lemma with the roles exchanged ($U_a=pp'(Y_a)$, $U=pp'(Y)$, $f_a=g_a$, $\sigma_a=\varepsilon_{Y_a}^{-1}$, $\varphi=\varepsilon_Y^{-1}$; indeed $pp'(g_a)\circ\varepsilon_{Y_a}^{-1}=\varepsilon_Y^{-1}\circ g_a$) shows that $\{g_a\}$ is a covering. This proves (1). Consequently the data $(p',p,\varepsilon^{-1},\eta^{-1})$, with $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal C$ exchanged, satisfy all hypotheses of the lemma: $p'$ is an equivalence preserving and reflecting coverings, with quasi-inverse $p$ and natural isomorphisms $\varepsilon^{-1}:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\cong p\circ p'$, $\eta^{-1}:p'\circ p\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$.

proof.text: *Step 2 ($p$ preserves fibre products).* By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] (with $F=p'$, $G=p$, $\alpha=\varepsilon^{-1}$, $\beta=\eta^{-1}$), $p$ is a right adjoint of $p'$. Let $T\to V\leftarrow V_a$ be morphisms of $\mathcal A$ whose fibre product $P=T\times_VV_a$ (with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$) exists; it is the limit of the diagram $T\to V\leftarrow V_a$ indexed by the category $\{1\to0\leftarrow2\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits], $(p(P),p(\mathrm{pr}_1),p(\mathrm{pr}_2))$ is a limit of $p(T)\to p(V)\leftarrow p(V_a)$, i.e. a fibre product $p(T)\times_{p(V)}p(V_a)$ in $\mathcal C$. Hence this fibre product exists, and the canonical morphism $p(T\times_VV_a)\to p(T)\times_{p(V)}p(V_a)$ (to any chosen fibre product, the morphism with components $p(\mathrm{pr}_1),p(\mathrm{pr}_2)$) is the comparison between two limits of the same diagram compatible with the projections, hence an isomorphism.

proof.text: *Step 3 ($p$ is continuous).* Let $\{V_a\to V\}_{a\in I}$ be a covering of $\mathcal A$. (a) $\{p(V_a)\to p(V)\}_{a\in I}$ is a covering of $\mathcal C$ by the hypothesis on $p$. (b) For a morphism $T\to V$ of $\mathcal A$ the fibre products $T\times_VV_a$ exist (axiom (iii) of 00VH) and the canonical morphisms $p(T\times_VV_a)\to p(T)\times_{p(V)}p(V_a)$ are isomorphisms by Step 2. So $p$ is continuous (Sites, Definition 00WV, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)).

*Step 4 ($p^s$ and $p'^s$ are quasi-inverse equivalences).* By Step 3, and by Step 3 applied to the data $(p',p,\varepsilon^{-1},\eta^{-1})$ of Step 1, $p$ and $p'$ are continuous; by [lem-weil-pbc-site-continuous-pushforward-sheaf] (Sites, Lemma 00WW), $p^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ p$ is a sheaf of sets (resp. abelian sheaf) on $\mathcal A$ for every sheaf of sets (resp. abelian sheaf) $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal C$, and $p'^s\mathcal F=\mathcal F\circ p'$ is one on $\mathcal C$ for every $\mathcal F$ on $\mathcal A$; on morphisms $p^s\psi=(\psi_{p(X)})_X$, $p'^s\phi=(\phi_{p'(Y)})_Y$, so both are functors. For a sheaf $\mathcal G$ on $\mathcal C$ we have $p'^sp^s\mathcal G=\mathcal G\circ p\circ p'$, and the maps $\mathcal G(\varepsilon_Y):\mathcal G(Y)\to\mathcal G(pp'(Y))$ are bijections (group isomorphisms), with inverses $\mathcal G(\varepsilon_Y^{-1})$; they are natural in $Y$ by naturality of $\varepsilon$ and functoriality of $\mathcal G$, and natural in $\mathcal G$ because morphisms of sheaves are natural transformations. So they form a natural isomorphism $\mathrm{id}\cong p'^s\circ p^s$ of functors on sheaves on $\mathcal C$. Likewise the maps $\mathcal F(\eta_X):\mathcal F(p'p(X))\to\mathcal F(X)$ form a natural isomorphism $p^s\circ p'^s\cong\mathrm{id}$ on sheaves on $\mathcal A$. Hence $p^s$ and $p'^s$ are quasi-inverse equivalences of categories (Categories, Definition 001J), on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves. This proves (2) (with Step 3) and (3).

source.place: Lemma Tag 00WW (lemma-pushforward-sheaf, line 2548); categories.tex Definition Tag 001J; written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 5 ($p_s$ is a quasi-inverse of $p^s$).* By Step 4 the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction] (Sites, Lemma 00WX) holds for $u=p$, so $p_s$ is a left adjoint of $p^s$ on sheaves of sets, resp. on abelian sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint] applied to the quasi-inverse pair $(p^s,p'^s)$ of Step 4, $p'^s$ is both a left adjoint and a right adjoint of $p^s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] with $R_1=R_2=p^s$, $\delta=\mathrm{id}$, $L_1=p_s$, $L_2=p'^s$ (uniqueness of left adjoints) there is a natural isomorphism $c:p_s\xrightarrow{\sim}p'^s$. Then $p^s\circ p_s\cong p^s\circ p'^s\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $p_s\circ p^s\cong p'^s\circ p^s\cong\mathrm{id}$ (whiskering $c$ and composing with the isomorphisms of Step 4), so $p_s$ is a quasi-inverse of $p^s$, on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves.

source.place: Lemma Tag 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves, line 2579); written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 6 ($p_s$ is exact; $p$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$).* On sheaves of sets, $p_s$ is a left adjoint of $p^s$ (Step 5), so by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits] it commutes with all colimits that exist, in particular finite ones. $p'^s$ is a right adjoint of $p^s$ (Step 5), so by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-limits] it commutes with all limits that exist. For a finite diagram in $\Sh(\mathcal A)$ with limit cone $\lambda$, the cone $p_s(\lambda)$ is isomorphic through the components of $c:p_s\cong p'^s$ (Step 5) to the limit cone $p'^s(\lambda)$, and a cone isomorphic to a limit cone is a limit cone; so $p_s$ commutes with finite limits. Hence $p_s$ is exact (Categories, Definition 0034), and the continuous functor $p$ (Step 3) defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal C\to\mathcal A$ (Sites, Definition 00X1, [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3)).

proof.text: *Step 7 (the same for $p'$).* By Step 1 the data $(p',p,\varepsilon^{-1},\eta^{-1})$ satisfy the hypotheses of the lemma with $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal C$ exchanged. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 6 applied to them give: $p'$ is continuous, $p'_s$ is a quasi-inverse of $p'^s$ (on sheaves of sets and on abelian sheaves), $p'_s$ on sheaves of sets is exact, and $p'$ defines a morphism of sites $\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$. Together with Steps 1-6 this proves (1)-(4).
